job.title: Grower Relations Manager - Fixed Term Contract
job.description:
The Company

Grains Research and Development Corporation (GRDC) is responsible for planning, investing in and overseeing research, development and extension (RD&E) for Australia's grains sector. Working closely with growers and industry, GRDC invests in research and extension that improves productivity, profitability and sustainability across Australian grain production systems.

The Opportunity

GRDC is seeking a Grower Relations Manager to strengthen regional industry engagement and support the delivery of RD&E investments that address grower priorities. Reporting to the Senior Regional Manager and working within the Grower and Stakeholder Engagement team, you'll connect directly with growers, advisers and the organisation. This is a varied role combining industry engagement, technical understanding and investment management, with the opportunity to influence regional priorities and manage investments that deliver practical outcomes for Australian grain growers.

Please note this role will be offered as a fixed term contract. 

This involves:
  • Building strong relationships with growers, advisers and industry stakeholders
  • Identifying regional challenges and opportunities to inform RD&E investment priorities
  • Developing investment proposals that will lead to meaningful research, development and extension for Australian grain growers
  • Representing GRDC at relevant field days, workshops and events
  • Managing RD&E investments, including contracts, budgets and delivery milestones
  • Monitoring investment outcomes and representing GRDC across regional industry networks
About You

To be successful in this role you will have:
  • Sound knowledge of Australian grains and broadacre cropping systems
  • Experience in agronomy, agricultural research, extension, industry engagement or related fields
  • Strong relationship-building skills and confidence engaging with growers and industry stakeholders
  • The ability to communicate technical information clearly to different audiences
  • Strong analytical, organisational and written communication skills
  • The ability to manage projects, competing priorities and detailed documentation
  • Commercial awareness and an interest in RD&E investment and contract management
  • A proactive, adaptable approach and willingness to develop new skills
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in agriculture, agricultural science or a related discipline
Importantly, GRDC is seeking someone who understands the grains industry, enjoys working with people and can bring together technical knowledge and practical industry needs.

The role involves regular regional travel, including overnight stays during peak industry activity periods.

Why This Role
  • Move beyond individual farms or portfolios and influence outcomes across the grains industry
  • Have a genuine say in regional research priorities and where RD&E investment is directed
  • Work closely with growers, researchers and industry leaders on challenges that matter
For confidential enquiries and a copy of the position description, please contact Charles Linton on 1300 380 701 or apply via rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: General Manager of Supply Chain
job.description:
The Company
Our client is a leading, large-scale horticultural business with integrated operations across farming, advanced packing facilities, cold storage, and domestic and export distribution. With a diverse multi-season operating footprint, the business is focused on operational excellence, sustainable produce supply, and continued growth.

The Opportunity
Reporting directly to the Chief Commercial Officer, this newly created executive position is based in regional Victoria. As General Manager of Supply Chain, you will own the end-to-end supply chain execution from crop estimate to final customer delivery encompassing fruit storage, packing schedules, procurement and freight.
As a central pillar of the commercial leadership team, you will establish and run a disciplined, binding S&OP / IBP process, bridging farm operations, packing facilities, sales and marketing.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Accountable for the design, cadence, and output of the S&OP / IBP process across all commodities and sites, maintaining a single aligned plan spanning harvest, packing, cold storage and demand.
  • Establishing allocation rules that align crop packout curves with market windows, customer commitments, and packaging formats, while reducing product directed to juice and minimising waste.
  • Owning and managing total cost-to-market per tonne across freight, packaging, dry goods, internal cartage and third-party logistics against budget baselines.
  • Overseeing procurement governance, competitive tender processes, contract registers, rate reviews and supplier performance across major spend categories.
  • Managing domestic and export logistics across sea and air freight, including protocol market compliance (DAFF requirements, orchard and packhouse accreditations and cold chain standards).
  • Managing controlled atmosphere store loading, sealing, release decisions, and container/pallet pooling arrangements to preserve shelf life and outturn quality.
  • Establishing master data governance across core systems, building advanced reporting and decision support capabilities, and elevating the supply chain from reactive execution to a scalable, best-practice operating model.
About You
The ideal candidate will be a commercially astute, data-driven supply chain leader who performs effectively in a fast-paced, seasonal environment and can maintain a clear, evidence-based position when priorities compete or operating pressure increases.
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in Supply Chain Management, Planning, Business, or an aligned discipline.
  • A minimum of ten years of senior supply chain leadership experience within FMCG, fresh produce, food processing, meat, dairy, or cold-chain environments.
  • Proven experience designing, implementing, and running mature S&OP / IBP processes in a multi-site setting.
  • Deep technical capability across domestic and international logistics, export market protocols, cold-chain management and procurement governance.
  • Strong analytical, data-reconciliation, and critical-thinking skills (proficiency with MS Office and BI tools such as Power BI or Tableau).
  • Outstanding cross-functional leadership and communication skills, with the ability to influence farming, site operations, and commercial sales teams alike.
  • High resilience, adaptability, and an operational focus on continuous improvement and bench-strength building.
Why This Role
This is a high-impact leadership opportunity to shape and scale an end-to-end agricultural supply chain, build organisational capability, and deliver measurable improvements in service, cost, quality, and operational resilience.
For a confidential discussion, contact Charles MacCallum on 1300 380 701 . Applications can be submitted via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Sales Agronomist
job.description:
The Company
Our client is an established agricultural business supplying high-quality products, technical expertise and practical support to farmers, rural retailers and industry partners across Australia. With a strong commitment to research, innovation and customer outcomes, the business offers an extensive portfolio of proven products supported by an active pipeline of new solutions. A collaborative culture, respected market presence and commitment to sustainable agricultural productivity underpin its continued growth.

The Role
This autonomous, field-based position will be responsible for managing an established, and further developing, an important Southern Queensland territory. The region offers flexibility around location and may suit candidates based across the Darling Downs, Toowoomba, Brisbane, the Gold Coast, Sunshine Coast, Fraser Coast or surrounding agricultural areas.

You will build trusted relationships with rural retailers, producers, agronomists, consultants and industry groups, combining agronomic support with disciplined territory and business development. Working with an established portfolio and new product pipeline, you will identify the right product fit for local farming systems, support customers with practical technical advice and create sustainable commercial growth.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Developing and executing territory plans to achieve sales, margin and growth objectives
  • Managing and expanding relationships with existing customers while identifying new business opportunities
  • Providing practical agronomic, product and farm-system support to retailers, advisers and producers
  • Positioning existing and new products within local pasture, forage and mixed farming systems
  • Coordinating field demonstrations, retailer training, industry events and other promotional activities
  • Monitoring seasonal conditions, customer needs, competitor activity and market opportunities
  • Maintaining effective territory planning, customer records, reporting and market intelligence
  • Collaborating with technical, sales and marketing colleagues to deliver strong customer outcomes
The Person
This opportunity will suit a commercially minded agricultural professional who enjoys working with customers, translating technical information into practical recommendations and taking ownership of a territory. You may already be working in agronomy, agricultural sales, rural retail, farm advisory, account management, product development or a related customer-facing role.

Experience across pasture, forage, seed, livestock production, cropping or broader farm inputs would be valuable, but candidates with strong transferable agricultural knowledge and the ability to build credibility with producers and channel partners are encouraged to apply. Formal qualifications in agriculture, agronomy, science or business will be well regarded but are not essential where supported by relevant industry experience.

You will bring:
  • A sound understanding of agriculture and the ability to learn and communicate technical product information
  • Strong relationship-building, communication and influencing skills
  • A proactive, organised and commercially focused approach
  • The confidence to work independently while contributing to a geographically dispersed team
  • Good territory planning, time management and follow-through
  • A willingness to travel regularly throughout Southern Queensland
  • Current Australian work rights and a valid driver’s licence
On Offer
This is an opportunity to take ownership of an established and strategically important territory with the backing of a respected agricultural business, a strong product portfolio and experienced technical and commercial colleagues.

A competitive salary package will be offered, including a fully maintained vehicle, phone and laptop, together with flexibility around where you are based within the region.

To discuss this opportunity confidentially, please contact Ryan Hoiberg at Rimfire Resources on 1300 380 701, or apply with your current resume and a brief outline of your relevant experience.

job.title: Discharge Supervisor
job.description:
The Company
Fertiglobe is a global leader in nitrogen-based solutions, supplying essential fertilisers that support agriculture and a more sustainable future. In Australia, its integrated manufacturing, blending, storage and distribution network serves major agricultural sectors across the east and southern coasts.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Shipping Manager, the Discharge Supervisor will plan, coordinate and oversee bulk fertiliser vessel discharges across eastern Australia. Based primarily in Port Melbourne, the role combines office-based planning and stakeholder coordination with targeted port attendance to deliver safe, efficient and cost-effective vessel turnarounds.

You will manage discharge plans, schedules, contractors and changing operational conditions. Active discharges require time-sensitive support outside standard hours, including some early mornings, evenings and weekends.
Additional key responsibilities include:
  • Develop discharge plans and monitor vessel movements, port activity and warehouse readiness.
  • Coordinate shipping agents, stevedores, transport providers, warehouse operators and internal teams.
  • Analyse performance, address delays and improve contractor, time and cost outcomes.
  • Maintain oversight of safety, product integrity, environmental obligations and regulatory compliance.
  • Complete operational reporting and attend ports as required.
The Person
We are seeking a commercially minded logistics professional with sound judgement, strong stakeholder skills and a clear focus on safety, service and efficiency.
  • Experience in vessel discharge, port logistics, stevedoring, transport coordination, shipping agency or a related environment.
  • Strong planning, analytical and problem-solving capability.
  • Knowledge of OHS, Chain of Responsibility, maritime safety and environmental compliance.
  • Commercial awareness, attention to detail and confident stakeholder communication.
  • A current driver’s licence and willingness to travel to ports and operational sites.
Why this role?
This newly established role offers genuine ownership of discharge outcomes and the opportunity to improve contractor performance and operational decision-making across Fertiglobe’s Australian supply chain network. Practical onboarding will be provided, with responsibility growing in line with capability.

For further information or an initial confidential discussion, please call Ryan Hoiberg on 1300 380 701. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Plant Operations Manager
job.description:
The Company
GenTech Seeds is a recognised premium brand in Australian agribusiness and the exclusive producer and distributor of Pioneer® brand products in Australia.

The business works closely with growers to produce hybrid seed products suited to Australian farming systems, with a major seed production and distribution facility based at Narromine in Central West NSW.

The Opportunity
This newly created role will take responsibility for the day-to-day operations of the Narromine facility, providing leadership across seed processing, bulk operations, treat and pack, warehousing and distribution.

Reporting to the Head of Production Operations, you will lead the operational teams and Production Leads, with a focus on people, planning, performance and ensuring seasonal production targets are achieved.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Lead day-to-day plant operations across processing, warehousing and distribution.
  • Manage production planning, labour, resources, workflows and competing priorities.
  • Set clear expectations and drive performance against operational targets and KPIs.
  • Lead, coach and develop the operational team, building capability and accountability.
  • Work closely with Quality, WHS, Maintenance and other site functions.
  • Identify opportunities to improve safety, quality, productivity and reliability.
While Production Leads manage much of the daily execution, you'll remain closely involved in the operation, providing direction, resolving issues and stepping in where needed. This role will suit a practical, hands-on leader who is equally comfortable managing people and priorities as they are getting involved on the plant floor.

About You
You’re an experienced operational leader who enjoys being close to the people and the day-to-day workings of a production environment.

Experience in seed processing or agriculture would be valuable, although GenTech is open to candidates from manufacturing, processing, grain handling, warehousing or other relevant production environments.

You will bring:
  • Experience leading operational teams in a production or processing environment.
  • Strong planning and organisational skills across people, workflows and resources.
  • A practical understanding of plant operations, safety and operational risk.
  • Confidence leading through supervisors or team leads and managing performance.
  • A practical, hands-on leadership style, with the willingness to step in and support the team when needed.
  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach across teams.
Why This Role?
This is a newly created position with genuine ownership of the day-to-day operation of an important production facility.

You’ll inherit an established team and step into a role with broad responsibility across people, production and site performance, while working closely with an experienced Head of Production Operations.

For someone who enjoys leading people, improving how a site operates and working in a practical production environment, the role offers considerable scope to make an impact within an established national seed business.

How to Apply
For a confidential discussion, contact Marcela Rocha Lima on 1300 380 701.

job.title: Research Agronomist
job.description:
The Company:
An exciting opportunity for a motivated Agronomist to join the Seed, Research & Development team based in Wagga Wagga, NSW. Reporting to the Breeding Operations Lead, this role will be instrumental in supporting canola breeding and variety evaluation programs across Southern NSW and Northern Victoria.

Working within a highly motivated and collaborative team, you will be involved in all aspects of field-based canola research, helping to develop the next generation of varieties that deliver value to Australian growers.

The Position
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Working with growers to identify and secure suitable field trial sites.
  • Packing, sowing, maintaining and harvesting canola variety evaluation and nursery experiments.
  • Applying agricultural chemicals safely and effectively.
  • Collecting and recording accurate field data.
  • Maintaining trial records and research documentation.
  • Operating and maintaining small plot research equipment and modern GPS-guided machinery.
The Person
To succeed in this role, you will ideally possess:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Agriculture, Agricultural Science or a related discipline.
  • Previous agronomy experience, ideally within broadacre cropping systems.
  • Experience operating agricultural machinery and precision agriculture technology.
  • A current driver's licence and willingness to travel throughout Southern NSW and Northern Victoria.
  • Strong communication, analytical and organisational skills.
  • The ability to work both independently and as part of a small, high-performing team.
  • A proactive approach to problem-solving and continuous improvement.
The Opportunity
This is a fantastic opportunity to join a respected agricultural research organisation at the forefront of crop innovation. You will enjoy a varied and hands-on role, working closely with growers and researchers while contributing to the development of improved canola genetics for Australian agriculture.

To Apply
For a confidential discussion, contact Charles MacCallum on 1300 380 701. To apply, visit www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Grains Buyer
job.description:
The Company
Our client is an industry leader in the manufacture of high-quality stockfeed products, supplying customers across Victoria and Southern New South Wales. With a multi-site feed mill network, strong operational capability and a reputation built on safety, quality and consistency, this Australian-owned agribusiness continues to invest in its people, systems and assets to support long-term growth and strengthen its market position

The Opportunity
Working closely with the Grains team leader, you will be responsible for the end to end management of grain contracts and grain procurement, with direction and support to purchase the required raw materials to ensure ongoing production across all facilities. You will be directed regarding approved suppliers and pricing elements to successfully negotiate and purchase products, and then be responsible for overseeing all relevant documentation and contract management.
In this role you will:
  • Negotiate and manage all commodity contracts, from execution to payment and conclusion
  • Manage internal grain inventory levels at each site tracking raw material inventory, usage and forecast requirements
  • Execute Grain Movement Orders
  • Manage and track all contract draw downs and grain storage handling facilities
  • Maintain relationships with grain trade suppliers and develop new business where possible
  • Evaluate and recommend suppliers/vendors
  • Provide market information relating to position and product quality relevant to raw materials to ensure wider team is across market trends and information.
About You
To be successful, you will have a close affinity to the Australian commodities sector, ideally relevant tertiary qualifications in an agricultural or economics degree as well as knowledge of grain contract and supply chain systems. You ideally will have 3+ years experience in the grains sector in a relevant role to give you an understanding of the major stakeholders and supply routes, with a high level of communication and attention to detail.

In return, you will be provided with a unique opportunity in the industry, working with a close knit, experienced team and an opportunity to work immediately in a commercially active role to contribute to a growing business. This is a head office role with limited flexibility to WFH to ensure the success in the role. To confidentially discuss this role, please call Ryan Hoiberg on 1300 380 701 or apply now via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Vice President, Go-to-Market - Australia & New Zealand
job.description:
The Company:

The Semios group is one of the world's leading independent providers of agtech solutions that helps growers, advisers and agricultural enterprises to improve planning, collaboration and decision-making. It is their mission to enable those involved in production agriculture to improve performance and minimize risk by connecting information to essential decisions.

An opportunity has arisen for an accomplished commercial leader to drive the growth and market success of the Agworld platform across Australia and New Zealand. With responsibility for commercial strategy, direct sales execution, channel development and market adoption, this role carries clear accountability for revenue growth and regional P&L performance.

job.title: National Sales Manager - Australia
job.description:

Our client operates in the Australian crop protection market, working with distributors, agronomists, advisers and growers to connect its product portfolio with the needs of Australian farming systems. Its commercial approach brings together national sales coverage, strategic customer partnerships and collaboration across marketing, technical, regulatory and supply chain functions.

Reporting to the Country Head, you will be hands on yet lead Australian sales strategy and execution, with a team of nine. To be successful in this position, we are seeking the following:
  • Significant commercial sales experience in Australian agriculture, crop protection, agricultural inputs or a closely related market.
  • Demonstrated hands on experience leading, coaching and developing geographically dispersed sales teams.
  • Strong retail distributor relationships and experience managing strategic customers, national accounts and commercial negotiations.
  • Commercial acumen across sales strategy, pricing, margin management, budgeting and forecasting.

  • A collaborative, accountable approach, with strong cross-functional communication skills and willingness to travel nationally.
  • Qualifications in agriculture, agribusiness or business are desirable.
Why This Role

Take ownership of national sales strategy while remaining close to customers and Australian agriculture. With nine direct reports and access to the Country Head, you can shape commercial priorities, make this job your own and develop team capability and influence product launches, channel partnerships and business growth.
  
For a confidential conversation please call David Jackson on 1300 380 701 or apply with a cover letter addressing the advertisement criteria and a current resume.

  • HR compliance and employment-related requirements
  • Improving HR processes and making them simpler and more consistent
  • Supporting managers to deal confidently with people matters
  • Ensuring HR initiatives are followed through and delivered
There will be plenty to manage, but also the opportunity to improve how things are done. You’ll need to be comfortable moving between the detail and the bigger picture, whether that means working through an employee issue, improving a process, checking documentation or helping a manager navigate a difficult conversation.

About you
We’re looking for someone who has solid HR experience but doesn’t need a highly structured corporate environment around them.
You’ll ideally be:
  • Hands-on and delivery focused with a strong bias towards action
  • Organised, methodical and good at following things through
  • Strong on HR process, governance and compliance
  • Commercial and pragmatic in the way you approach HR
  • Approachable and capable of building relationships across all levels

  • Confident dealing with sensitive or challenging people matters
  • Able to bring structure and discipline without making things unnecessarily bureaucratic
  • Comfortable working independently and using good judgement

job.title: Head of Innovation & Business Development
job.description:
The Company:

DataGene is an independent, industry-owned organisation helping Australian dairy farmers make better decisions through data, technology and science.
We sit at the intersection of dairy farming, industry data, technology and research. Our work includes national genetic evaluation and genomic services, industry data infrastructure, decision-support tools and software services designed to improve the productivity, profitability and sustainability of Australian dairy businesses.

DataGene is entering an exciting period of growth and evolution, with opportunities to increase adoption of its existing services, develop new data-driven products and build commercial and strategic partnerships across the dairy industry.

The Position:

The Head of Innovation and Business Development is a newly created senior role responsible for leading DataGene's customer-facing innovation, business development and industry adoption activities.

This is fundamentally a commercial and customer-focused leadership role. You will work closely with dairy farmers, member organisations, advisors, commercial businesses and industry partners to identify opportunities, develop compelling propositions and turn ideas into products, services and partnerships that deliver measurable value.

A key focus will be building and progressing commercial and strategic partnerships, developing business cases for new opportunities, and increasing uptake of DataGene's existing and emerging products and services.

Many of DataGene's customers are reached through intermediary organisations—including genetics businesses, herd-testing organisations, veterinarians, consultants and industry advisors—so experience building effective partnerships and driving growth through indirect channels will be particularly valuable.

You will also lead a small team spanning stakeholder engagement, communications and product management, and work closely with DataGene's science and technology teams to translate customer and market needs into clear priorities.

You do not need to be a geneticist or herd-improvement specialist. We are looking for someone who understands the Australian dairy industry, is curious about technology and data, and has the commercial judgement and leadership capability to identify opportunities and turn them into outcomes.

The Person:

To be successful in this demanding but highly rewarding role, you will possess the following key skills and background:

Essential:
  • Demonstrated experience in business development including identifying and progressing growth opportunities, partnerships and/or new product offerings through indirect channels
  • Strong commercial acumen and proven experience developing business cases and assessing strategic fit, value and feasibility of new opportunities
  • Demonstrated leadership experience with the ability to build and develop capability in others
  • Demonstrated ability to build credibility and influence with senior external stakeholders and represent an organisation effectively in industry settings
  • Experience in developing, delivering or selling data-driven or technology-enabled products and services
  • Experience translating customer and market insight into product requirements and priorities
  • Strong understanding of how to drive adoption, customer value and measurable uptake beyond stakeholder engagement alone
  • Ability to operate at both strategic and operational levels in a player-coach capacity
  • Strong knowledge of the dairy value chain (producer through to processor and retail)
Highly Desirable:
  • Established dairy industry relationships
  • Experience working with veterinarians, consultants, advisors or agricultural intermediaries
  • Experience building or leading product management functions
This is an outstanding newly created opportunity to play a key role in assisting in the evolution of DataGene’s genetics and breeding technologies and farm data strategy.

If you have a genuine passion for business development, ideally with exposure to the Australian Dairy, then in the first instance, please call Mick Hay or David Jackson on 1300 380 701 for an initial discussion or further information. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Regional Manager - Crop Research
job.description:
The Company
Our client is a leader in providing science based, agricultural field research services, conducting trials in the major broadacre and horticultural cropping regions of Australia. With offices and staff strategically positioned, providing a full suite of services, they are focussed on helping advance new technologies to market and developing new agricultural inputs and systems.

With experienced staff and working with leading edge technology, business is based on creating great relationships with clients, so they are committed to open and consistent communication.

The Role
A role has become available for a Regional Manager - Young to manage an area of the central business research unit, overseeing the field operations and logistics in the broadacre regions of central and southern NSW.

Reporting to the Eastern Business Manager, you will be responsible for managerial, technical and administrative areas of the unit’s business performance. This includes working closely with your team of 6 direct reports to ensure delivery of clients and trial objectives. The research work is comprehensive and diverse covering a wide range of crops across residue, efficacy and breeding trials.  It is estimated that 60% of your time would be in the office and 40% in the field, which would include training newer staff and running your own small field trial program.

There is a requirement to travel at regular intervals to nearby regional offices.

The Person
The successful person will have the following skills and attributes:
  • Commercial business & people management experience.
  • Agronomy knowledge and familiarity with crops grown in this geographic region.
  • Ideally field trial (R&D) and logistics experience, with good attention to detail.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Agriculture/ Business /Commerce.
A generous salary package including vehicle is on offer for the successful candidate. This location is based in Young NSW.

You may have local industry experience in crop protection, seed, retail distribution, research or Research Development Corporations (RDC’s), and looking for a new challenge to step up into a leadership role.

 Come and join a leading research agribusiness bringing your business and people management skills. The skilled and dynamic team is growing, accumulating a wealth of experience, providing learning opportunities around the country.

Please call Al Kellaway on 1300 380 701 for a discussion and copy of the Position Description, or apply via www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Territory Manager & Product Development Manager - Central Queensland
job.description:
The Company
Terranova Seeds is a specialist vegetable seeds company with more than 40 years’ experience. They supply commercial growers across Australia and New Zealand with a wide range of vegetable varieties and technical support. The business also exports selected products to the USA, SE Asia, PNG, the Pacific Islands, and customers in Europe, Africa, and Central America.
  
Partnering with leading international breeding companies, Terranova Seeds has grown consistently and become a market leader. With experienced technical staff, they provide high‑quality seed solutions trialled under local conditions to ensure reliability. The company is known for exceptional service, strong client relationships, and ongoing growth both locally and globally. Quality of product is their mantra.

The Opportunity  
Reporting to the National Sales Manager, this is a unique role that does not come along often. A hybrid function combining your sales and client management skills with product development responsibilities.
  
Your product development function will focus on the ongoing development of new products in the wider Queensland, gathering robust trial data forecasting and maintaining supplier relationships for existing and potential new commercial lines. You will do this by working closely with the National Product Development Manager, overseeing product development across the region as required while being highly connected to the end user, suppliers and client base in the supply of specific vegetable seed products. Focusing on crops such as tomatoes, peppers, cucurbits, green bean and sweetcorn. Overall, you are pivotal to delivering the desired products to an established and loyal client base while building a pipeline of products to introduce to growers in the future.  
  
Your sales focus is about business development. You will be to grow and develop revenue and gross profit within the region by sourcing and driving sales opportunities within the existing client base, while targeting new business clients for Terranova. Your selling skills and ability to influence and convert sales is vital for this role.   
  
You will:
  • Grow sales, volume and gross profit in the region to targets
  • Be present in the region looking for growth opportunities with existing and new clients
  • Spend the majority of your time client engaged developing sales and product development
  • Oversee ongoing trialling, development and launch of new vegetable varieties
  • Gather and report quality trial data to support new varieties (so you will be hands on)
  • Work closely with the product development team and sales team nationally to forecast sales, supply and inventory needs
About you

To be successful in this role you will ideally have:
  • Proven sales skills and experience in a similar environment
  • Technical experience in the vegetable seed industry and a sound knowledge of agronomy
  • Direct experience in running ongoing vegetable trial programs and reporting outcomes
  • Strong report writing skills with accuracy/attention to detail supported by exceptional written and verbal communication skills
  • A natural ability and experience to listen and work positively with clients, suppliers, and growers
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications
Terranova offer a positive work culture where you will be provided with generous salary package including base, superannuation, car, phone, laptop and participate in the Company’s bonus plans. You will be expected to undertake local and international travel.

This is a unique opportunity with Terranova; an agile specialist vegetable seeds company which delivers tailored and ethical service delivery to its clients. A place where you have the flexibility to make decisions and lead by example yet work in a team environment.
   
For a confidential conversation please call David Jackson on 1300 380 701 or apply with a cover letter addressing the advertisement criteria and a fresh resume.
